title: New Factor Elara is an aero-optimised gravel race bike with 57mm tyre clearance
content:
Cyclist
New Factor Elara is an aero-optimised gravel race bike with 57mm tyre clearance

Factor has launched its latest gravel bike, the Elara. It’s the third new gravel bike from Factor in the past year and is designed to supersede the Ostro Gravel, with Factor claiming it is ‘the purest expression of fast gravel’.

While the Aluto aims for all-rounder gravel performance at a more affordable price and the Sarana is designed for ultra-endurance gravel racing, the new Elara is at the pointy end of gravel race design and looks to carry on where the Ostro Gravel left off, adopting the latest trends in gravel race bike design.

Road race bike responsiveness and handling

According to Factor, the Elara is ‘a new fast gravel racing bike engineered around a clear objective: deliver the handling and responsiveness of a road race bike without compromising the capability demanded by modern gravel racing‘.

Factor emphasises the Elara’s agile handling, with the bike’s geometry ‘intended to reward aggressive positioning and decisive inputs, giving riders the confidence to attack corners, accelerate out of turns and hold speed across rapidly changing terrain’.

At the same time, the Elara has the big tyre clearance now expected from gravel race bikes, allowing you to fit 57mm rubber, 12mm more than the Ostro Gravel and just 1mm less than the Sarana. Factor says that this isn’t about comfort though; it’s to help riders maintain speed and traction, manage impacts and improve puncture protection.

Factor claims its updated gravel race geometry helps keep the handling responsive despite the wider tyres and that the Elara is unique in offering such wide clearance while keeping the chainstay length down to 423mm.

Other aspects of the Elara’s geometry have been updated too. Relative to the Ostro Gravel, there’s a longer frame reach, reduced trail and lower bottom bracket with around 80mm drop. Factor claims this helps plant the rider within the bike to a greater extent and is more akin to a road race bike than the more relaxed geometry typical of a gravel bike.

At the same time, Factor says that the Elara is designed to maintain stability on loose, uneven surfaces and fast descents. Head tube angle is over 72 degrees across larger frame sizes and the seat tube angle is between 74 and 75 degrees.

The frame also allows you to choose either a 1x or 2x groupset, with 52-tooth chainring capacity in 1x configuration. Fitting 2x does reduce tyre clearance to 47mm though. To accommodate this has needed a thinner driveside chainstay, which is also dropped, with Factor adopting a monocoque design that it says results in better frame alignment and a lower weight, with a size M raw frame claimed to weigh under 1,100g.

In-frame storage allows you to carry gear out of the wind and full builds are fitted with shorter cranks of between 165mm and 172.5mm in length. 

Aero optimisation based on Factor One and Ostro VAM

Along with clearance, a modern gravel race bike also needs to be aerodynamically optimised. 

Factor says it has leaned on its road bike tech, offering a wide stance fork that looks similar to that of the Factor One, a narrow head tube and aero down tube shapes, resulting in aero efficiency that it says its CFD analyses and wind-tunnel validation indicate is on a par with road bike frames. 

There are drag reductions despite the wide tyres and Factor claims the Elara’s drag is up to 8% less than the Ostro Gravel when fitted with 47mm tyres.

The Elara comes fitted with a new aero bar/stem from Black Inc with a 17 degree flare, available in stem length/bar width combos from 80mm/360mm to 140mm/400mm.

Higher specs come with new Black Inc Sixty Four Gravel wheels, designed to complement the frame’s aerodynamic performance and support the wider tyres, thanks to a 30mm internal width, as well as including ceramic bearings and fast freehub engagement. Factor claims a 1,620g wheelset weight.

Factor Elara specs and prices

Factor will sell the Elara in six frame sizes from 49 to 61cm and with a zero or 20mm setback seatpost. The Elara frame package is priced at £5,899 / $5,999 / €7,199.

Full builds range in price from £8,999 / $9,199 / €10,999 with Force XPLR AXS and Black Inc 46 wheels to £10,999 / $11,399 / €13,599 with Red XPLR AXS and the new Black Inc 64 wheels.
